content.title: Generation Y
content.text: Generation Y, also known as Millennials , are a demographic cohort that falls between Generation X and Generation Z . People in this age group were born throughout the 1980s through to the mid-1990s and are most often the children of Baby Boomers . Generation Y currently comprises the largest labor force share (36%) in the US. At the end of 2025, the Generation Y age range will be between 29 to 44. Generation Y were born between the years 1981 and 1996. Generational cohorts are defined by a specific range of birth years. Researchers create these groups based on historical, economic, and social factors. A study by the Population Reference Bureau considers whether they should be known as the “unluckiest generation” due to the onslaught of historical events and turmoil they have lived through. Yes. Gen Y is the same as Millennials. Gen Y and Millennials can be used interchangeably to describe people born between 1980 and 1996, though the specific date range can vary depending on location. These employees are accustomed to frequent feedback and may respond well to online recognition systems. The group born after Generation X was initially coined Gen Y because it was the next letter progression in the current naming schema. However, this demographic is more commonly called Millennials, as the oldest members became adults at the turn of the Millennium. While Millennials and Gen Y are still used to describe this age cohort, the Millennials label has gained more popularity and recognition in media, gradually replacing Gen Y within the US. However, in other parts of the world Gen Y may be used more frequently. Like all generations, Gen Y has unique characteristics that need to be managed accordingly. Millennials are considered one of the most educated generations. Millennial women, in particular, are 44% more likely to complete a college education. Having come of age with the internet and smartphones, Gen Y are pretty tech-savvy. This cohort was the first to grow up with widespread access to the Internet, smartphones, and other digital technologies. Generation Y was significantly impacted by the Great Recession of 2008 , so their financial independence has had some unique challenges. Their starting wage earnings are lower than those of some previous generations (when adjusted for inflation), making Gen Y more likely to live with their parents for longer, rent, and delay major life events than previous generations. Companies need to work harder to engage their younger workers. According to Gallup, this cohort is more likely to be actively looking for new job openings elsewhere than other generations.
